headline: Approved 99 Sears Island Drive home addition; $2,000 fine at 342 Lake Avenue; 2 New Bond Street hearing continued.
summary: Members approved an order for a home addition at 99 Sears Island Drive and issued a negative determination for diesel cleanup at 100 C Street. They approved a $2,000 fine for work near a wetland at 342 Lake Avenue and set new deadlines for several enforcement orders. The hearing on turf and playground work at 2 New Bond Street was continued to November 16th.
decisions: Continued the public hearing for 1 & 3 Suburban Road to December 7th, 2026, and extended the deadline to December 29th, 2026, 5-0.
Issued a negative determination for diesel fuel cleanup at 100 C Street, 5-0.
Approved orders of conditions for an addition and deck at 99 Sears Island Drive, 5-0.
Continued the hearing on field and playground work at 2 New Bond Street to November 16th, 4-0, with one member recused.
Approved a partial certificate of compliance for 84 Chester Street, 5-0.
Approved an invalid certificate of compliance for Lot A, New York Street, 5-0.
Approved a certificate of compliance for 135 Goddard Memorial Drive, 5-0.
Approved a certificate of compliance for 190 Brookline Street, 5-0.
Approved an amendment to the enforcement order for 13 Holden Street requiring the restoration plan prepared by Matt Marro, 5-0.
Approved an amendment to the enforcement order for 34 Eskow Road and 224 Southwest Cutoff allowing basin work with a May 15th deadline, 5-0.
Approved a fine of $100 per day for 20 days, $2,000 total, against Lakeview Property, LLC for work near wetlands at 342 Lake Avenue, 5-0.
Approved an amendment to the enforcement order for 342 Lake Avenue to show the fine, 5-0.
Approved an amendment to the enforcement order for 88 Webster Street requiring a Notice of Intent by January 6th, 5-0.
Approved an amendment to the enforcement order for 142 Olean Street requiring the work discussed, including removal of the pool platform, 5-0.
discussion: Ordinance and regulation updates: Staff described proposed changes to streamline permits, add climate resilience standards, and protect isolated vegetated wetlands. Staff aim to send the ordinance to City Council by the end of the calendar year.

142 Olean Street pool platform: Members said the pool platform is in the 30-foot no-structure buffer and must come out. The owner said the platform would be removed this fall, with bank plantings next spring.

2 New Bond Street turf: Members asked how old turf and crumb rubber would be removed and whether the new mesh fence would let floodwater pass. Members said late-submitted materials needed review, so the hearing was continued.
88 Webster Street riprap: Crews pulled back the riprap and found concrete and metal underneath. Members said the bank must be permitted if it stays, and they set a January 6th filing deadline.

Enforcement fines policy: Members asked for a clear policy on when fines start and whether orders can go to court or criminal referral. Staff agreed to bring a policy and check with the Law Department.
